testing_centers.notes: Available at Pearson VUE test centers worldwide

id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. ID must match the name on the exam registration. Acceptable forms include passport, driver's license, or national ID card.
exam_rules: Open-book exam. Physical and electronic notes are permitted — building a comprehensive index is a key preparation strategy. No internet access during the exam except to pre-loaded approved materials. Proctored at Pearson VUE centers or online via ProctorU. Candidates have a 4-month window to schedule and take the exam after registration.
renewal_options: Certifications are valid for 4 years. Renewal requires 36 CPE (Continuing Professional Education) credits earned over the 4-year period, plus a $429 renewal fee. Alternatively, candidates may retake the current exam to renew.
target_audience: Practitioners responsible for intrusion detection, system analysts, security analysts, network engineers and administrators, hands-on security managers
recommended_experience: Not specified in the provided content.

prerequisites.description: Hands-on experience in intrusion detection, network monitoring, traffic analysis, and intrusion detection systems.

retake_policy.notes: Two free practice tests are included with each exam registration. Candidates have a 4-month window to take the exam after registration. Retake fees apply after the first failed attempt. Contact GIAC for specific retake waiting periods.

domains.name: Fundamentals of Traffic Analysis and Application Protocols

objectives.title: Application Protocols
sub_objectives: Demonstrate knowledge and skill relating to application layer protocol dissection and analysis.

domains.name: Open-Source Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS): Snort and Zeek

objectives.title: IDS Fundamentals and Network Architecture
sub_objectives: Demonstrate knowledge of fundamental IDS concepts, such as network architecture options and benefits/weaknesses of common IDS systems.

objectives.title: Intrusion Detection System Rules
sub_objectives: Create effective IDS rules to detect varied types of malicious activity.

objectives.title: Network Forensics and Traffic Analysis
sub_objectives: Demonstrate competence in analyzing data from multiple sources (e.g., full packet capture, netflow, log files) to identify normal and malicious behaviors.

domains.name: Concepts of TCP/IP and the Link Layer

objectives.title: Concepts of TCP/IP and the Link Layer
sub_objectives: Demonstrate understanding of the TCP/IP communications model and link layer operations.

objectives.title: Fragmentation
sub_objectives: Demonstrate understanding of how fragmentation works, and how to identify fragmentation and fragmentation-based attacks in packet captures.

objectives.title: IP Headers
sub_objectives: Demonstrate the ability to dissect IP packet headers and analyze them for normal and anomalous values that may point to security issues.

objectives.title: IPv6
sub_objectives: Demonstrate knowledge of IPv6 and how it differs from IPv4.

objectives.title: Packet Engineering
sub_objectives: Demonstrate knowledge relating to packet crafting and manipulation.

domains.name: SiLK and Other Traffic Analysis Tools

objectives.title: SiLK and Other Traffic Analysis Tools
sub_objectives: Demonstrate an understanding of SiLK and other tools to perform network traffic and flow analysis.

objectives.title: TCP
sub_objectives: Demonstrate understanding of the TCP protocol and the ability to discern between typical and anomalous behavior.

objectives.title: Tcpdump Filters
sub_objectives: Demonstrate ability to craft tcpdump filters that match on given criteria.

objectives.title: UDP and ICMP
sub_objectives: Demonstrate understanding of the UDP and ICMP protocols and the ability to discern between typical and anomalous behavior.

objectives.title: Wireshark Fundamentals
sub_objectives: Demonstrate ability to use Wireshark to analyze typical and malicious network traffic.
